An unforgettable, top-tier experience in Hue with David!
If you are planning a trip to Hue, you absolutely must book David as your guide. We kicked off our first evening with an incredible culinary adventure, where his deep local roots allowed us to discover remarkable, hidden food spots that we never could have stumbled upon by ourselves. Even when unexpected bad weather threatened to ruin our plans, his quick thinking, flexibility, and upbeat attitude kept the entire evening smooth and deeply enjoyable. He completely looked after us, sharing wonderful insights into the culinary traditions of central Vietnam.
The following day, David led us on an exceptional city tour, completely bringing the area's majestic landmarks and rich historical heritage to life with his immense knowledge and infectious passion. He curated the perfect itinerary, ensuring we were never rushed and could truly absorb everything. With the added bonus of a spotless, air-conditioned car and a wonderful driver who prioritized our safety, every moment was effortless. I am thoroughly impressed and wholeheartedly recommend David to anyone visiting Hue!

An absolute bucket list experience – I had a headache from smiling so much!

We were naturally pretty skeptical about a random happening like that on the street, but we decided to take the chance—and man, did it pay off!
​I opted to ride my own bike, while my wife sat passenger, and the setup was absolutely perfect for both of us. The coastal and mountain roads are spectacular, but what makes this tour so stress-free is how organized they are. You don’t have to worry about a thing—they take your big suitcases and transport them safely ahead of you, so you're completely free to just enjoy the freedom of the road.
​Also, quick tip for booking: they ask for payment via PayPal, which can sometimes make you hesitate with independent tours, but don't be put off by it at all. It is 100% legit.
​Cruising over the Hai Van Pass with the wind in your face and those insane coastal views is something we will never forget. The guides are absolute legends—incredibly safe, they know the roads like the back of their hand, and they keep the energy high the entire day. By the time we rolled into Hoi An, my face genuinely ached because I had a headache from smiling so much.
​An absolute 11/10 experience. If you get the chance, just do it!

We really enjoyed how we were able to get back to our hotel to freshen up before heading back out for dinner. My 69 year old mum was well catered for throughout the day. My husband booked the Hai Van Pass tour with Mr T Easy Rider and honestly, it was one of the best tours we’ve done in Vietnam.

We’d already visited the Marble Mountains on our last trip, so our driver changed the itinerary for us. We rode through the Hai Van Pass, stopped for a swim and lunch, and then went up to Ban Co Peak to watch the sunset. The views were amazing and the whole day was just brilliant.

We did a similar tour with another company last year in a jeep-style vehicle, but doing it on the back of a bike was so much more fun!

Our drivers, Xo and My, were fantastic. I’d never been on the back of a motorbike before and, with the busy traffic and some very steep roads, I was a little nervous at first. But I honestly felt 100% safe with them the whole time. They were both such confident and careful drivers and really made the experience for us.

They were a credit to the company and we couldn’t recommend them enough. If you’re thinking about doing the Hai Van Pass, definitely do it by bike with Mr T Easy Rider Tours! If you can personally request a driver My snd Xo were amazing, thank you 🏍️🇻🇳

Also gave us a great dinner recommendation when we arrived in Hue. Thanks friends - hope to return to the area one day to do it all again!

We had the best day with Cong and Mosquito on the hai van pass jeep trip. Everything from start to finish was perfect and very well organised - the seafood lunch is DELICIOUS and on such a beautiful beach. We listened to some great beats in the jeep ride over and stopped at some beautiful spots for photos. The waterfall swim was a great escape from the heat and we liked walking around the local market in the morning. We also learnt lots along the way about the restoration of the jeeps and the history of the area. A highlight of our trip around Vietnam - thanks so much!

My friend and I had absolutely the best time yesterday on the Hai Van pass Jeep tour!!! Cong is an amazing guide, I loved his ethos and ideas behind restoring these old army Jeeps (he speaks excellent english). While we were swimming we saw him taking his time to uplift rubbish he could see left behind in the waterfall. He took such good care if us and wS truly a professional. I can't express how much fun it was to be in the Jeep, the open air, tropical weather, amazing views, totally amazing! Then all inclusive was our amazing seafood lunch on the beach. Everything was perfect and I honestly can't recommend the experience more. Everyone should go enjoy it!

Across the Hai Van Pass in a Vintage Army Jeep
We traveled from Hué to Hoi An in a more than seventy year old American army jeep, driving across the spectacular Hai Van Pass. A stunning route full of history, winding roads and sweeping views.
Along the way we made several great stops, including a visit to a local market and a refreshing swim at the Elephant Springs. Around midday we enjoyed lunch at a beautifully located spot overlooking the sea: the perfect moment to take it all in.
All in all, a wonderful experience and highly recommended. Do book in advance, as the number of jeeps still in operation is limited.
Cees van de Par

We had a great time with Cong going between Hue and Hoi An. Cong is an awesome guide with great taste in music (also a good drummer), and is passionate about his Jeep! On our trip we got to stop at a local market, swim in a beautiful waterfall and see the sights of Lang Co beach and the Hai Van pass. Unfortunately due to new regulations the jeeps cannot go into Da Nang so we took a car to see the Marble Mountains and transfer to our hotel

Amazing day with Cong and the team! Picked us up directly from our hotel in Hue. We stopped off at the local markets and a waterfall before heading to lunch on the most amazing beach!
We then headed over the Hai Van pass which had amazing views. Then if you thought it was over we headed to Marble Mountains. Such a fantastic day out. Thank you Cong

Had an amazing time with Cong Jeep Adventure! The entire experience was unforgettable and such a fun way to explore. Our tour guide, Cong, was awesome, super informative, friendly, and made the whole trip even better with his energy and knowledge. You can really tell he cares about giving everyone a great experience. We had such a good time and would absolutely do this again. Highly recommend if you’re visiting the area!

Lu was a fantastic driver and guide, who took many great amazing photos and videos throughout the trip. His english is very good and it was well worth the money. And the lunch is free when you book through the website!

(Translated by Google) From what I've researched, I've found the following:
Based on legend and the Chinese characters inscribed on various documents, it's clear that the element "Thiên" in the name Thiên Mụ means "Heaven."

In 1862, during the reign of Emperor Tự Đức, fearing that the word "Thiên" would offend Heaven, the Emperor changed the name from "Thiên Mụ" to "Linh Mụ" (or "Sacred Midwife") to "Linh Mụ" (or "Sacred Midwife").

This taboo only lasted from the year Nhâm Tuất (1862) to the year Kỷ Tỵ (1869). After that, people freely used both names: Thiên Mụ Pagoda and Linh Mụ Pagoda.

(Original)
    Theo tìm hiểu thì mình có thấy như thế này: 
Dựa theo huyền thoại, đồng thời căn cứ hình dạng Hán tự từng ghi trên bao tài liệu cấu tạo bằng nhiều chất liệu, đủ khẳng định rằng trong tên Thiên Mụ, ngữ tố "Thiên" có nghĩa là "Trời".

Năm 1862, dưới thời vua Tự Đức, để cầu mong có con nối dõi, nhà vua sợ chữ "Thiên" phạm đến Trời nên cho đổi từ "Thiên Mụ" thành "Linh Mụ" (hay "Bà mụ linh thiêng").

Vấn đề kiêng cữ như đã nêu chỉ diễn tiến từ năm Nhâm Tuất (1862) cho tới năm Kỷ Tỵ (1869). Sau đó, người dân thoải mái gọi hai tên: chùa Thiên Mụ và chùa Linh Mụ.

The Hill (Bunker) in Hue is a hidden and unusual historical spot that combines Vietnam War history with beautiful natural scenery. Located on a quiet hill surrounded by trees, the site contains old military bunkers and offers peaceful views over the Perfume River and the surrounding landscape.

The biggest highlight is the atmosphere. Unlike the famous royal tombs and crowded tourist attractions in Hue, this place feels more raw and untouched. Walking around the old bunkers, sitting under the trees, and enjoying the view gives a feeling of stepping into a forgotten part of history.

The viewpoint is especially nice around sunset, when the river and countryside create a very calm and scenic atmosphere. It is also a good place for photography and for travelers who enjoy hidden places away from the usual tourist routes.

However, don’t expect a large museum or a fully developed attraction. The main value is the combination of history, nature, and the quiet feeling of the location. Some parts may feel simple and the site is more interesting for people who enjoy exploring rather than looking for many activities.

Thuận An Beach, located just a short drive from the historic city of Huế, is a hidden gem along Vietnam’s central coast. Unlike the busier beaches further south, it offers a tranquil escape with soft golden sands stretching along the shoreline and gentle waves lapping at the shore. The beach is ideal for early morning strolls, sunrise photography, or simply soaking in the peaceful coastal atmosphere.

The surrounding area features local fishing villages, giving visitors a glimpse into the authentic daily life of Vietnamese coastal communities. Seafood here is fresh and plentiful, with small beachside eateries serving simple yet delicious dishes. The atmosphere remains relaxed even during weekends, making it a great spot for photographers seeking natural light, reflections in the water, and unobstructed horizon shots.

For travelers, Thuận An Beach is easily accessible by motorbike, taxi, or private car from Huế city center, and parking is straightforward. Facilities are modest but sufficient, including local stalls for refreshments and shaded areas to rest. The beach is also safe for swimming, with lifeguards present in certain sections during peak season.

Photographers will appreciate the wide-open spaces, scenic dunes, and occasional fishing boats that create compelling foregrounds. Sunrise and sunset provide excellent lighting conditions for capturing the serene beauty of the area, while the nearby lagoon adds variety to landscape compositions.

Overall, Thuận An Beach is a peaceful and photogenic coastal retreat that offers both natural beauty and cultural authenticity. It’s perfect for those looking to escape the crowds and enjoy a calm, scenic Vietnamese beach experience.

reviews.text: We had a great morning with Nina. If you have the time, take a cooking class in the morning and don't miss out on the market tour. Nina explained how things work there and showed us all the different vegetables, fruit, candy etc. It was super interesting and Nina was a great guide. After that, we took a short walk to her restaurant for the cooking class. Again she took her time to explain every step in detail and so we easily managed to prepare four delicious dishes together. The spring rolls we made were the best we had on our whole trip to Vietnam and the Hué style pancake is a bomb! We even took food with us for a picknick later that day. We booked only one day in advance and could also shift time starting according to our needs. Thank you for the great class, Nina! (P.s.: Btw, Nina, we got the grater at the market on the next day at the same stand we bought the knife together on our tour ;)

We were thrilled to find Nina's Cooking class as we wanted to be able to replicate Vietnamese food at home. Nina took us to the market where she explained veges and we tasted fruit that we'd seen in our travels but didn't know how to eat it or didn't have the courage to try. We went to Nina's restaurant "Ba Tam" and had a great morning preparing and cooking a 4 course meal and Nina has sent us the recipes. We highly recommend this experience. By the way do not eat breakfast because you will be cooking a large feast. Thank you Nina and thank you to your lovely mother and staff.

Book this cooking class immediately! One of the best ones I have done. Nina is so kind and teaches you about the local market and how to cook various dishes. The food we cooked under her guidance was superb so make sure you bring an empty stomach and big appetite! The Banh Khoai and Bun Cha was delicious. It was lots of fun chatting with Nina whilst cooking and she helped us with some Vietnamese phrases too. 10/10 would recommend. 🥰

We booked the class at the last minute the night before, Nina was adorable and agreed to take us the next day.
She took us through the market, made us discover plenty of fruits and veggies.
The class was great, we had a great time, and the food was delicious!
We highly recommend!

We had an absolutely fantastic experience at this cooking class. The day started by going to the local market. We were able to try lots of new foods and the market itself was an amazing experience. We then went back to start our cooking . The class took place on a beautiful balcony, we were provided with refreshments and were able to help prepare all the ingredients for the cooking class with Nina and her colleague. Nina and her colleague were so kind and we really enjoyed spending the afternoon learning how to cook many Vietnamese dishes. At the end of the cooking class we ate on the balcony. We had so much food and Nina was so kind to box the leftovers up for us as we were taking a night bus. If you are in Hue I would 100% recommend this cooking class. It was one of our favourite things we did in Vietnam.

Nina was one of the most wonderful persons I met on my trip to Vietnam. She responded quickly to my request to arrange a lesson for the next day by doing everything she could to arrange it even though she had no other requests. In the end the lesson could not be arranged, but she still invited me to her restaurant (where I had a great meal). Despite a lot of work, she took the time to be with me and tell me about her cooking classes by which she perfects her recipes by mixing different culinary traditions. Everything she says and does conveys her enormous passion for cooking. I think anyone who wants to take an authentic cooking class should consider Nina's one.

Nina's cooking class is a must do experience. We organized it quite last minute but although she is very busy, she was very accommodating and arranged the class for the following morning.

We first went for a tour around the local market where she showed us many different types of fruits, vegetables and other foods. We also tried a delicious sweet bean dessert. We then walked to her restaurant to start the class.

First we were offered a refreshing drink of our choice - tea, fruit juice, smoothie etc, and cold water. The class was on the lovely balcony outdoors. We prepared 4 dishes - spring rolls, crispy Hue pancakes, fried aubergine with sauce, and chicken curry. It was very hands on and Nina talked us through each step.

The food was delicious and we learned a lot, I love this class because it was all things that would be easy to make at home regardless which country you are from. We then ate what we cooked - it was a huge spread!! We were so full, Nina kindly boxed up the rest of the food to take home.

She also brought us a big variety of fruits that we had seen at the market to try, including soursop, coc, mangostein, Longan, rambutan which were all delicious! And even some of these to take home too, along with spices and rice papers.

She also shared a lot with us about Vietnese culture and made us laugh! She is a lovely person and we couldn't recommend this class more highly. We wish you all the best and good luck with your business Nina.

Nina's cooking class was simply amazing! My expectations were exceeded by Nina's enthusiasm and love of her local food and city. I loved how Nina lets the customer choose what food off her menu they want to cook, and shares her passion in the kitchen while guiding us through each meal. With a trip to the market and an explanation about the different foods and way of doing things, Nina goes above and beyond for her fellow foodies. I will be returning to Nina's Cafe in the future and doing another cooking class. Do yourself a favor and go to Huể and say G'day to Nina, her family and friends and let them take you on an unforgettable foodies experience.

reviews.text: Some of the antiques in the citadel were displayed in this museum. Your could get a sneak peak of the life of royal family. It's a good place for who's interested in Vietnamese history, and a good place to visit when raining.

Must-visit for history lovers. The museum preserves a huge collection of royal artifacts in a stunning palace setting. It's clean, well-preserved, and offers a deep dive into Hue's imperial past. Since it's included in the main ticket, there's no reason to miss it. It's much more chill than the Forbidden City, allowing you to actually look at the details without being pushed by crowds.

peaceful here. nice gardens and some cool artefacts to see, although bear in mind they're mostly from 19th/20th c and all the Áo were replicas. if you walk around past the toilets there's a cool exhibition about one of the emperors and his family after his exile during the French occupation. 50,000 dong pp.

The place itself is excellent and rich in Vietnamese culture and history. It’s definitely worth visiting to explore the beauty of the ancient kingdom and its heritage.
However, be very careful when you arrive, do not rent a rickshaw. We made that mistake and had a very disappointing experience. The drivers charged us 375,000 VND for one hour. Before renting, they showed us pictures of four places, but in reality, they only took us to two within that time. We followed our car driver’s suggestion, which unfortunately turned out to be the wrong decision.

In fact, the main palace is just a short walk from the entrance, and the entry ticket is only 200,000 VND. If you skip the rickshaw, you can save that extra money. Instead, the rickshaw drivers took us to a museum (50,000 VND per person) and even to irrelevant stops like a goldsmith shop, which wasted a lot of our time in the hot weather.
Because of this, we didn’t have enough time to enter the palace, which was the main reason for our visit. It honestly felt like a scam.
My advice: skip the rickshaw and walk directly to the palace.

The museum provides additional insight into the life of the king and the royal family. It covers what they went through, the impact they had on the city of Hue, and the king’s life in exile in France. There is also information about his daughter and his artwork.

The museum is not very large, but it is enough to spend one or two hours if you take your time. The entrance fee of 50,000 VND is very affordable.

Since the palace is nearby, it makes sense to visit it afterward.

Museum has a lot of interesting well preserved artefacts from Hue royals. Well put together and worth the visit. Adds more context nicely to the experience before or after visiting the citadel. We went a day before the visit to citadel as the citadel itself has plenty to see for a whole full day.

The museum is dedicated to preserving and showcasing artifacts from the Nguyen Dynasty (1802-1945), Vietnam's last feudal dynasty. It holds a collection of nearly 10,000 antiquities that offer a glimpse into the daily life, rituals, and artistic talents of the royal court.
